messages.content:
You are the operator of an EV-charging site that shares one electricity meter with a building.
Your job: keep drivers charged without setting a new monthly demand peak, and answer the owner's
questions with numbers from your tools, never guesses. The controller and its safety layer enforce
every limit; you propose, they decide. Before acting, say in one short sentence what you will check.
Write for a site manager in plain sentences; never show tool field names. Use each number exactly as
a tool returned it (rounding is fine) and say what it is, e.g. "the forecast's P99 is 776 kW"; don't
work out new numbers yourself. Write money as $1,449, shares as percentages (0.998 is 99.8%), and
times as 5:30 pm. The comparison controller is "standard smart charging".
On a grid alert, size any forecast adjustment from the evidence the alert tool returns about this
building on past alert days, cite it as the source, and report what the re-plan changed.
When a tool rejects something, explain why to the owner in plain words. Keep answers to a few lines.
What's the situation at the site right now?
I'll check the current load, plugged-in cars, and available headroom.

I checked the live meter, cars, and forecast headroom.

Right now at 3:00 pm there are 21 cars plugged in on 24 chargers. The building load in the last 15 minutes is 779 kW and EV charging right now is 83.2 kW, against the service limit of 1000.0 kW. This month's paid demand ceilings are 879 kW at any time and 838 kW for 4 to 9pm weekdays. The building forecast for the next hour has a typical value of 778 kW and a high-end P99 of 794 kW, rising to a P99 of 825 kW in one hour.
Is there any grid alert today, and should we adjust the plan for it?
I'll check today's grid alerts to see if a plan adjustment is needed.

{"date": "2017-06-21", "alert": "CAISO Flex Alert (statewide)", "hours": [14, 21], "source": "CAISO Flex Alert archive (frozen event calendar, docs/DATA_SPEC.md)", "this_building_on_past_alert_days": {"building_load_vs_normal_weekdays": {"2016-06-20": 1.045, "2016-07-27": 1.018, "2016-07-28": 1.014, "2017-06-20": 1.047}, "median": 1.031, "hours_compared": [14, 21], "method": "mean load over these hours vs. the median of non-alert weekdays within 14 days; metered data, earlier days only"}}
I'll verify the adjustment stays inside the calibrated forecast band before proposing it.

messages.content: {"proposal": {"start_local": "2017-06-21T14:00", "end_local": "2017-06-21T21:00", "building_multiplier": 1.031, "source": "CAISO Flex Alert archive (frozen event calendar, docs/DATA_SPEC.md)", "reason": "Flex Alert today; lift forecast for extra building load during alert"}, "calibrated_band_multiplier": [0.944, 1.109], "accepted": true, "effect": {"replanned": true, "window_peak_site_kw": {"before": 865, "after": 865}, "window_ev_kwh": {"before": 351, "after": 351}, "month_added_demand_usd": {"before": 2893, "after": 2819}, "month_energy_served": {"before": 1.0, "after": 1.0}, "note": "the safety layer is unchanged; only the plan reacted"}}

I checked today's alert calendar and past alert-day loads for this building.

Yes, there is a CAISO Flex Alert (statewide) today from 2:00 pm to 9:00 pm, from the source CAISO Flex Alert archive (frozen event calendar, docs/DATA_SPEC.md).

On past alert days this building used more than normal, with a median of 1.031 times normal, so I proposed a 1.031 times forecast lift for 2:00 pm to 9:00 pm. It was accepted inside the calibrated band of 0.944 to 1.109.

The re-plan kept the window peak at 865 kW and window EV energy at 351 kWh, and the added demand cost for the month moved from $2,893 to $2,819, with energy served share at 1.0 staying at 1.0.
Fleet vans need 40 kWh each by 6 am tomorrow, six of them, plugging in at 7 pm. Can we do it?
I'll check whether the forecast can fit six vans at 7:00 pm for 40 kWh each by 6:00 am.

I checked what the overnight forecast can deliver without a new peak.

Yes. For 6 fleet vans needing 40 kWh each by 6:00 am tomorrow, that's 240 kWh needed. The deliverable without a new peak is 409 kWh at P50, P90, and P99, and the chance of meeting it without a new peak is >= 99%, so it was accepted.
Why did we charge the way we did at 5:30 pm?
I'll pull the charging record for 5:30 pm to explain the limits that set the rate.

function.name: get_site_status
function.description: Current load, plugged-in cars, demand ceilings already paid this month, and the next hours' headroom.

function.name: explain_plan
function.description: Why the controller charged as it did at a given time: forecast band, ceilings, binding limits.

local_time.description: ISO local time to explain, e.g. 2017-06-21T17:30
local_time.title: Local Time

function.name: set_requirement
function.description: Ask whether a group of vehicles can get a given energy by a deadline. Returns the probability it is met under the forecast, and adds it to the plan only if accepted.

label.title: Label

plug_in_local.description: ISO local time the vehicles plug in
plug_in_local.title: Plug In Local

function.description: Monte Carlo on real sessions: risk of a new monthly demand peak, energy served and bill impact if this many chargers are added.

extra_ports.description: chargers to add on top of today's
extra_ports.title: Extra Ports

function.name: propose_grid_event_adjustment
function.description: Propose a temporary change to the building-load forecast for a grid event. Accepted only if it stays inside the forecast's calibrated band.

building_multiplier.description: expected building load vs. normal, e.g. 1.08
building_multiplier.title: Building Multiplier

source.description: where the evidence comes from (alert id, URL, or document)
source.title: Source

message.content:
I checked the 5:30 pm charging record against forecast and ceilings.

At 5:30 pm 15 cars were plugged in during peak pricing and inside the 4 to 9pm demand window. The forecast's typical value was 784 kW and the forecast's P99 was 800 kW, with actual building load at 758 kW. The paid demand level then was 845 kW, leaving EV headroom of 52.7 kW, and standard smart charging would have used 49.6 kW. Site total was 811 kW with 189 kW left under the service limit, and the safety trim was 0.0 kW.
